{{short description|Italian physicist (born 1965)}}
'''Giovanni Amelino-Camelia''' (born 14 December 1965, [[Naples]]) is an Italian [[physicist]] of the [[University of Naples Federico II]] who works on [[quantum gravity]].

He is the first proposer of [[doubly special relativity]],<ref>Amelino-Camelia: {{Citation|title=Relativity in space-times with short-distance structure governed by an observer-independent (Planckian) length scale|journal = Int. J. Mod. Phys. D | volume = 11 | date = 2002 | pages =  35–60 |arxiv=gr-qc/0012051|bibcode = 2002IJMPD..11...35A |doi = 10.1142/S0218271802001330 |last1 = Amelino-Camelia |first1 = Giovanni |last2 = Ahluwalia |first2 = D. V. |issue = 1 |s2cid = 16161466 }}</ref> that is the idea of introducing the [[Planck length]] in physics as an observer-independent quantity, obtaining a relativistic theory (like Galileian relativity and Einstein's special relativity). The principles of doubly special relativity probably imply the loss of the notion of classical (Riemannian) spacetime; this led Amelino-Camelia to the study of [[non-commutative geometry]] as a feasible theory of [[quantum spacetime]].
Amelino-Camelia is the initiator of "[[Phenomenological quantum gravity|quantum-gravity phenomenology]]", for being the first<ref>Amelino-Camelia et al.: {{Citation|title=Potential Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Burster Observations to Wave Dispersion in Vacuo |journal = Nature | volume = 393| date = 1998 | pages = 763–765 |arxiv=astro-ph/9712103|bibcode = 1998Natur.393..763A |doi = 10.1038/31647 | issue=6687|last1 = Amelino-Camelia |first1 = G. |last2 = Ellis |first2 = John |author-link2=John Ellis (physicist, born 1946) |last3 = Mavromatos |first3 = N. E. |author-link3=Nikolas Mavromatos|last4 = Nanopoulos |first4 = D. V. |author-link4=Dimitri Nanopoulos |last5 = Sarkar |first5 = Subir |s2cid = 15009076 }}</ref> to show that with some experiments under reach of current technology sensitivity to Planck-scale effects is feasible (see [[Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope]]).

==Biography==
After graduating in physics from [[University of Naples Federico II]] in 1989, he received his Ph.D. from [[Boston University]] in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.roma1.infn.it/~amelino/|title=Home Page of Giovanni AMELINO-CAMELIA|access-date=2007-05-21|archive-date=2009-04-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090419172048/http://www.roma1.infn.it/~amelino/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has held several postdoctoral positions abroad. From 2000 to 2018, he was a university researcher at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], where he taught “Introduction to Quantum Gravity.”<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://gomppublic.uniroma1.it/Insegnamenti/Render.aspx?UID=4ff8766a-c84a-4e0f-b127-0eadfcfcbbb8&CodiceInsegnamento=1041552&CodiceCurriculum=be27962f-109b-470c-96f0-1ed6441de0af&CodiceUT=cc6f8306-089b-4adb-aa72-d125a8c843dd |title=Introduzione alla Gravità Quantistica - Laurea Magistrale 2015/2016 |access-date=2025-08-06 |archive-date=2016-06-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160625070917/http://gomppublic.uniroma1.it/Insegnamenti/Render.aspx?UID=4ff8766a-c84a-4e0f-b127-0eadfcfcbbb8&CodiceInsegnamento=1041552&CodiceCurriculum=be27962f-109b-470c-96f0-1ed6441de0af&CodiceUT=cc6f8306-089b-4adb-aa72-d125a8c843dd |url-status=dead }}</ref> Since 2018, he has been a researcher at the [[University of Naples Federico II]]”, where he teaches "General Relativity and Gravitation".

[[Quantum gravity]] is concerned with the study of physical regimes in which both the effects due to [[Quantum mechanics]] and those of [[General relativity]] are no longer negligible, and aims at the development of unitary theories of gravitational phenomena compatible with both.  In this field, Amelino-Camelia is the proponent of doubly special relativity, a relativistic theory that stands as an evolution of Einstein's [[Special relativity]] and is based on the introduction of two relativistic invariants: the [[Planck units]] (minimum length scale) and the Planck energy (maximum energy scale). This approach was later developed by other authors, including [[Lee Smolin]].

A second contribution by Amelino-Camelia is simplified models of quantum gravity that can be experimentally verified with currently available technologies, such as the [[NASA]]-sponsored [[Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope]] for observing gamma-ray bursts and cosmic gamma rays.

The [[h-index]] of his publications is among the highest among those of active Italian theoretical physicists.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.it/citations?user=qm_z_gkAAAAJ&hl=it|title=Giovanni Amelino-Camelia}}</ref>

In 2008, the U.S. magazine [[Discover (magazine)]] included him in its list of 6 possible new [[Albert Einstein]] capable of operating a new physics revolution.

He is a member of the [[Accademia Pontaniana]] of [[Naples]] and the [[Foundational Questions Institute]] founded by [[Max Tegmark]].
